source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Ensure all the required equipment for measuring emissions is properly calibrated and functional.
3. Record baseline data before beginning the monitoring process.
4. Take continuous measurements over a significant period (e.g., one month).
5. Use advanced monitoring systems like stack monitors, continuous emissions monitoring systems (CEMS), or stationary air-quality sensors.
6. Check for exceedances of the allowable emission limits set by regulatory bodies (e.g., EPA, local air quality management districts).
7. Use appropriate units of measurement when documenting emissions (e.g., parts per million, grams per second).
8. Document the dates and times of monitoring along with the meteorological data (wind speed, temperature, humidity, etc.).
9. Verify all data with quality assurance and quality control procedures.
10. Disclose the industrial activities related to the emissions (e.g., combustion, chemical processing).
11. Record the methods used to mitigate emissions if any (e.g., scrubbers, filters
